bib.title: Semi-supervised sequence tagging with bidirectional language models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 55th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 1756-1765

question: Can context embeddings from a pre-trained bidirectional language model, added to a supervised sequence tagger, improve NER and chunking without extra labeled data?
hypothesis: Language model embeddings encode semantic and syntactic roles of words in context, so they should help a tagger whose RNN is trained on little labeled data.
contributions: Show that the context sensitive representation from LM embeddings is useful in supervised sequence tagging (CoNLL 2003 NER 90.87 to 91.93 F1; new state of the art 96.37 F1 on CoNLL 2000 chunking).
Show that using both forward and backward LM embeddings boosts performance over a forward-only LM.
Show domain specific pre-training is not necessary by applying a news-domain LM to scientific papers.

method.summary: TagLM: a hierarchical tagger (char CNN/RNN + pre-trained Senna word embeddings, two stacked bidirectional RNNs, CRF) whose first-layer output is concatenated with the frozen top-layer states of separately pre-trained forward and backward LSTM language models. Evaluated on CoNLL 2003 NER and CoNLL 2000 chunking, with ablations on NER.
method.task: sequence tagging (named entity recognition, chunking) with LM-embedding feature augmentation

datasets.name: CoNLL 2003 NER
datasets.split: standard train/dev/test; final models trained on train plus dev after tuning hyperparameters on dev
datasets.source: Reuters RCV1 newswire, four entity types (PER, LOC, ORG, MISC)
datasets.preprocessing: lowercase all tokens, replace all digits with 0; BIOES tags

datasets.name: CoNLL 2000 chunking
datasets.split: WSJ sections 15-18 train, section 20 test; 1000 sentences randomly sampled from train as dev
datasets.source: Wall Street Journal corpus, 11 chunk types plus other

datasets.name: 1B Word Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2014)
datasets.size: approximately 800 million tokens in training split (about 4000X the CoNLL training tokens)
datasets.source: public language modeling benchmark of news text

datasets.name: SemEval 2017 Task 10 ScienceIE
datasets.source: scientific publications from computer science, material sciences, physics; entity types Task, Material, Process

models.name: TagLM tagger (baseline, NER)
models.architecture: char encoder with two bidirectional GRUs of 80 hidden units and 25-dim char embeddings; sequence layer of two bidirectional GRUs with 300 hidden units; dense layer; CRF
models.init_from: Senna word embeddings (Collobert et al., 2011), fine tuned

models.name: TagLM tagger (baseline, chunking)
models.architecture: char CNN (30-dim char embeddings, 30 filters of width 3, tanh); sequence layer of two bidirectional LSTMs with 200 hidden units; dense layer; CRF

models.name: CNN-BIG-LSTM (forward LM)
models.architecture: char CNN with 4096 filters input, two stacked LSTMs each 8192 hidden units with 1024-dim projection
models.init_from: released by Jozefowicz et al. (2016); weights frozen

other.train_cost: three weeks on 32 GPUs (Jozefowicz et al.)

models.name: LSTM-2048-512 (forward and backward LMs)
models.architecture: token embeddings into single layer LSTM with 2048 units and 512-dim projection
models.init_from: trained by the authors on 1B Word Benchmark; weights frozen

models.name: LSTM-512-256 (small LMs on CoNLL 2003 only)
models.architecture: 512 hidden units with 256-dim projection, forward and backward
models.init_from: trained on CoNLL 2003 train+dev, normalized as tagger input

training.objective: sentence CRF loss (forward-backward) for the tagger; Viterbi decoding at test; LMs trained as forward/backward next-token prediction with softmax (removed afterwards)
training.lr: 0.001 constant, then divided by ten twice
training.lr_schedule: constant 0.001 until the epoch with best dev performance, then divide by 10 and train five epochs, divide by 10 again, train five more epochs and stop
training.epochs: early stopping on dev, then 5 + 5 annealing epochs; LSTM-2048-512 LMs trained 10 epochs
training.dropout: NER: 25% on input to each GRU, not recurrent connections. Chunking: 50% on char embeddings, input to each LSTM layer, and output of final LSTM layer
training.regularisation: dropout and early stopping; pre-trained LM weights fixed, Senna embeddings fine tuned
training.hardware: LSTM-2048-512 LMs: four GPUs, synchronous updates (GPU type not stated)
training.seeds: each final configuration trained ten times with different random seeds; mean and standard deviation of F1 reported

other.lm_insertion: LM embeddings concatenated with the output of the first bidirectional RNN layer, h_{k,1} = [fwd h; bwd h; h_LM]
other.lm_embedding: concatenation of forward and backward top-layer LSTM states, forward and backward LMs independent with no shared parameters

inference.decoding: Viterbi for most likely tag sequence
inference.samples: ten runs with different random seeds, mean and std F1

eval.protocol: Mean and std over ten seeds; significance by two-sided Welch t-test at 95% (p = 0.021 for NER vs 91.62 of Chiu and Nichols); for chunking p < 0.001 assuming standard deviation of 0.1 for the prior result.

availability.data: CoNLL 2003, CoNLL 2000, 1B Word Benchmark are public

evidence.quote: decrease α an order of magnitude (i.e., divide by ten), train for ﬁve epochs, decrease α an order of magnitude again, train for ﬁve more epochs and stop.

results.claim: Adding LM embeddings raises CoNLL 2003 NER test F1 over the same tagger without an LM.
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER test, TagLM with forward CNN-BIG-LSTM and backward LSTM-2048-512, LM embeddings at output of first RNN layer, trained on train+dev, no gazetteers or extra labeled data
results.quote: overall performance increases from 90.87% to 91.93% F1 for the CoNLL 2003 NER task

results.claim: TagLM sets a new state of the art on CoNLL 2000 chunking.
results.setup: CoNLL 2000 chunking test, two-layer bi-LSTM tagger with char CNN, same LMs, no additional labeled data
results.quote: We also establish a new state of the art result (96.37% F1) for the CoNLL 2000 Chunking task.
results.table: Table 2, row TagLM, column F1 ± std (96.37 ± 0.05; baseline 95.00 ± 0.08)

results.claim: The NER gain is statistically significant over the previous best result that used gazetteers.
results.setup: TagLM 91.93 vs Chiu and Nichols (2016) 91.62 ± 0.33 with gazetteers, CoNLL 2003 test

results.claim: Average absolute gain from LM embeddings on the chunking task is larger than for NER.
results.setup: CoNLL 2000 chunking, no-LM baseline 95.00 vs TagLM 96.37
results.quote: the LM embeddings amounts to an average absolute improvement of 1.06 and 1.37 F1 in the NER and Chunking tasks, respectively

results.claim: LM embedding gains exceed gains from gazetteers or transfer learning in prior work (e.g. +0.71 for gazetteers, +0.06 for transfer).
results.source: Chiu and Nichols (2016); Yang et al. (2017)
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER, Chiu and Nichols adding gazetteers; Yang et al. +0.06 from CoNLL 2000/PTB-POS transfer
results.quote: Chiu and Nichols (2016) reported an increase of 0.71 F1 when adding gazetteers to their base-

results.claim: Inserting LM embeddings at the output of the first RNN layer works best.
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER; alternatives: input to first RNN 91.55 ± 0.21, output of second RNN 91.72 ± 0.13
results.table: Table 5, row output of the first RNN layer, column F1 ± std

results.claim: Adding a backward LM beats forward-only, with the two-LM system best.
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER, forward LSTM-2048-512 alone 91.40 vs forward+backward LSTM-2048-512 91.62
results.quote: adding backward LM embeddings consistently outperforms forward-only LM em-
results.table: Table 6, row LSTM-2048-512 / LSTM-2048-512, column F1 ± std

results.claim: Larger forward LM (CNN-BIG-LSTM, perplexity 30.0) improves F1 about as much as adding a backward LM.
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER, forward-only CNN-BIG-LSTM vs forward-only LSTM-2048-512 (91.40)
results.quote: improves F1 by 0.26 - 0.31%, about as much as adding backward LM

results.claim: An LM trained only on the small CoNLL 2003 data slightly hurts relative to no LM.
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER; LSTM-512-256 forward and backward LMs trained on CoNLL 2003 train+dev, perplexities 106.9 and 104.2
results.table: Table 6, row LSTM-512-256*, column F1 ± std

results.claim: Removing the task-specific sequence RNN and using only LM embeddings plus dense layer and CRF is far worse than the baseline.
results.quote: performance was very low, 88.17 F1, well below our baseline

results.claim: With 1% of the CoNLL 2003 training set, the LM gain is larger.
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER, 1% of training set sampled following Yang et al. (2017)
results.note: Compared with +1.06 on full training data.

results.claim: Giving the no-LM baseline as many parameters as TagLM does not help; shrinking TagLM's second layer to baseline size slightly raises F1.
results.setup: CoNLL 2003 NER; no-LM with matched parameters was 0.15% F1 below baseline; chunking showed no such improvement

results.claim: A news-domain LM improves entity extraction on scientific text (ScienceIE).
results.setup: SemEval 2017 Task 10 ScienceIE development set, LM trained on 1B Word news text
results.quote: TagLM increased F1 on the development set by 4.12% (from 49.93 to to 54.05%)
results.note: Text prints 'to to' as a typo.

limits: Authors hypothesize but did not test that a backward LM as large as CNN-BIG-LSTM would improve performance further.
Alternative ways to combine LM embeddings (non-linear mapping, attention) were not explored.
News-domain LM and news-domain labeled data in the main evaluation; domain transfer tested only on ScienceIE dev set.
Parameter-matching conclusion is task dependent: a similar experiment for chunking did not improve F1.
Batch size, steps and hardware type for the tagger are not given; no code link for TagLM.
Dated: LSTM-based frozen feature extraction, superseded by fine-tuned transformers.

terms.definition: an encoding of the context at each position in the sequence computed by a pre-trained neural language model, used in the supervised tagging model
